identity.real_world_identity_notes: DTM homologation special built to beat the E30 M3 in the German championship. The 2.5-16 Evolution cars use a dog-leg five-speed Getrag manual in which first gear sits left and rearward, deliberately moved out of the racing shift plane, with a limited-slip differential.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
There is no automation: the clutch is needed to pull away, the driver lifts the throttle to upshift and blips it to downshift.

The dogleg gate was seen directly in the cockpit during the guided drive and is independently corroborated by the registered sources. First gear sits out of the racing shift plane, so second through fifth fall in one straight sequence.

The gearbox construction comes from the car's FIA Group A homologation form. Every five-speed the form homologates is marked synchronised, so whichever of them this car carried it was a synchromesh. The form also homologates six-speeds of other construction - one has a blank synchro column - which is why the gear count is what makes this answerable rather than a guess.

The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. It is recorded as optional rather than required, which is reserved for gearboxes that need it to engage. The guided drive recorded a downshift accepted after the driver blipped; it did not record one being refused without a blip, so nothing here says the simulator demands it. A drive that attempted an unblipped downshift would settle whether a simulator override belongs here.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mercedes-benz-190e-2-5-16-evo-ii-dtm.20260813t202923808z-ec6dd926 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: Registered sources establish the real-world identity and transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The sources establish a dog-leg five-speed Getrag manual, and the live drive confirmed five gears through an H-pattern gate observed as a dogleg. The guided drive observed the gate in the cockpit and reported an ordinary dogleg, with first down and to the left of the racing plane. The homologation form corroborates both from a primary source: article 603 tabulates five forward ratios, and 603 f) draws the gate with reverse above first and 1, 3 and 5 on the lower plane.

Every gearbox with five forward ratios homologated on this form is explicitly marked synchronised - the base Getrag, the additional gearbox on the same sheet, and the further five-speed added by extension. The form does homologate gearboxes of other construction, including one whose synchro column is blank throughout, but those are six-speeds and this car has five. So no choice is being made between permitted options: at five ratios they agree. The remaining step, from what the form permits to what this car was built with, is inferred rather than stated by the source, which is why this sits at medium and not higher.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
The guided drive recorded that the upshift was accepted after a throttle lift, with no automatic cut detected.

A synchromesh matches the shaft speeds itself, so the blip eases the synchros and is authentic technique rather than a requirement to engage the gear. This follows from the established construction rather than being stated by a source, and cannot be more certain than the construction it comes from. The guided drive is consistent with it: the downshift was accepted after a blip, and no unblipped downshift was attempted.

driver_summary: Getrag five-speed with a dogleg gate - first is down and left, outside the racing plane, so second through fifth fall in one straight fore-and-aft line.
